name: Lodha The World Towers
address: Lodha Place, Shankar Rao Naram Path / Senapati Bapat Marg, Lower Parel (marketed as Worli), Mumbai 400013
amenities: 7-acre landscape and ~100,000 sq ft entrance courtyard
description: A three-tower luxury complex of World One, World View and World Crest on the former Shrinivas Mills site in Lower Parel. Lodha announced it in June 2010 with World One billed as the world's tallest residential tower at 117 storeys. Aviation-height limits later capped World One at 280 m and 76 floors. The towers hold 3, 4 and 5 bedroom residences, and the interiors were designed by Giorgio Armani.
notes: Towers: World One (76 floors, 280.2 m), World View (73 floors), World Crest (57 floors), per Wikipedia and CTBUH. Land: 17 acres per Lodha's website and MahaRERA filings, which say 17.00 acres for both phases. Housing.com says 7 acres, which matches only the landscaped area. Total units are not stated because sources disagree: the MahaRERA phases show 61 units (P51900008345, World One Tier II) and 369 units (P51900008962, World One Tier III and Trinity), Square Yards says 445 units, and Dwello says 384. Possession dates: DNA (2018) reports buyers were told the project would be delivered in 2015, and the 2014 Lodha statement said completion was expected in 2016. The MahaRERA completion dates were 31 Dec 2017, revised to 30 Sep 2018 for Tier II (Square Yards also cites a later revision to 25 Feb 2020), and 30 Jun 2021 for Tier III and Trinity. possession_promised (2015) and possession_actual (2020) are year-only dates. The 2020 completion of World One is from Wikipedia and CTBUH. One MahaRERA complaint says an OC for some World One flats was obtained in July 2017, and a consumer complaint cites a Lodha letter of 24 May 2019 claiming the OC was received. Litigation: buyers (mostly corporates) moved MahaRERA in 2018, alleging the 117-storey marketing was misleading because the AAI cleared only about 285 m. Funding: HDFC Property Fund invested Rs 500 crore in 2010 for about 10% and exited in October 2016 for about Rs 1,500 crore. Piramal Fund committed Rs 2,320 crore in 2016. Notable buyers: Amrita Puri and parents (Rs 37 crore, 2025) and Nitin and Neil Nitin Mukesh (Rs 11.35 crore, 2025). Enrichment (Nov 2026): Architect, structural engineer (LERA), landscape designer (Ken Smith) and Armani/Casa interiors are per Lodha's World Towers and World One pages. Contractors are per Wikipedia (World One): Arabian Construction Co. and Simplex built World One, and Muscovite Group built World View and World Crest. flats_per_floor = 2 is World One ('only two residences on each landing', Lodha). lifts_per_tower = 18 is the elevator count Wikipedia gives for World One only. Views: Lodha describes panoramic city views and a tower rising above the city and the Arabian Sea; the estate borders Mahalaxmi Race Course, but a racecourse view is not stated, so it is left out. land_type is mill_land because the project sits on the former Shrinivas Mills site; tenure was not found. oc_received is set to true because the towers are occupied and marketed as ready (Lodha 'Status: Ready'; Square Yards 'Ready to Move'), and earlier complaints cite a July 2017 OC for some World One flats; no consolidated OC date was found, so oc_date is left out. units_sold (298) is computed from Square Yards' MahaRERA summary (Nov 2025): 240 of 249 launched units booked in the Tier III and Trinity phase (3 BHK 141 of 147, 4 BHK 99 of 102) plus 58 of 61 '4 BHK villa' units in Tier II. Square Yards notes the Nov 2025 and Jul 2024 figures are identical, so they may be stale. transactions_12m = 10 registered sales (about Rs 157 crore) from Nov 2025 to Oct 2026, per Square Yards' IGR summary for World One. Nearest metro: mumbaimetroroute.com lists Science Museum (Line 3) at 0.9 km, Worli and Siddhivinayak at 1.1 km and Acharya Atre Chowk at 1.7 km; these look like straight-line distances. Distances to BKC and the airport by road in km were not found (Lodha gives about 30 minutes by car to the airport). Maintenance: no project-specific rate was found; a Sep 2025 RP Realty Plus article puts Lower Parel luxury towers such as World One at roughly Rs 12,000-15,000 a month per 1,000 sq ft, too vague to record as a field. Research gap (Nov 2026 top-up): searches for 2019-2021 registered deals or Lodha price statements around possession, and for a launch price with a stated area basis, found nothing usable; Macrotech's offer documents report sales by company, not by project. PropertyButler shows only asking prices for World One / World Towers.
contractor: Arabian Construction Co. and Simplex (World One); Muscovite Group (World View, World Crest)

price_points.note: Soft-launch rate 'among select buyers' at Rs 25,000 a sq ft, as quoted in a search-engine excerpt of the June 2010 article. The full text could not be retrieved (HTTP 403), and a pre-launch price sheet on a blog lists Rs 23,000/sq ft for 3 BHK.

news.title: Lodha announces world's tallest residential tower
news.summary: Lodha announces World One at Lower Parel as a 117-storey, roughly 442 m tower on the former Shrinivas Mills land, costing about Rs 2,000 crore.

news.title: Lodha group sells Rs 500 crore worth flats in 9 days at Mumbai high-rise
news.summary: Bookings reopened on 29 Nov 2014 and drew about Rs 500 crore in nine days. Lodha said units would fetch upwards of Rs 70,000-80,000/sq ft, civil work was about 75% complete, and completion was expected in 2016.

news.title: Piramal Fund to invest Rs2,320 crore in Lodha's World Tower
news.summary: Piramal Fund Management commits Rs 2,320 crore to the World Towers project, partly to fund HDFC Property Fund's exit. The date is month-level, per Wikipedia's citation.

news.title: HDFC PE fund exits Lodha's World Tower project for Rs 1,500 crore
news.summary: HDFC Property Fund, which invested Rs 500 crore in 2010, exits for about Rs 1,500 crore, roughly three times its money.

news.title: DNA Money Exclusive: Lodha 'World One' buyers move RERA over tallest claim
news.summary: Buyers file MahaRERA complaints alleging World One was sold as 117 storeys without AAI height approval. Only about 285 m (around 76 storeys) was cleared, delivery was promised in 2015, and Lodha had collected Rs 1,830 crore by Dec 2017.

news.title: Actress Amrita Puri Buys Luxurious House In Mumbai's Lower Parel For ₹37 Crore
news.summary: Amrita Puri and parents Aditya and Anita Puri buy a 5,446 sq ft 49th-floor World One apartment for Rs 37 crore. The sale was registered in April 2025, with Rs 2.22 crore stamp duty.

news.title: Neil Nitin Mukesh & His Father Buy A Lavish Apartment In Mumbai's Lower Parel Worth ₹11.35 Crore: Report
news.summary: Nitin and Neil Nitin Mukesh buy a 2,044 sq ft (carpet) 31st-floor World One unit for Rs 11.35 crore. The deal was registered in July 2025 and reported in October 2025, so the date is month-level.
